channel.title: Livable Telluride — Weekly Digest
channel.description: This week's upcoming Gov-Hub meetings and community events across the Telluride region (Town of Telluride, Mountain Village, San Miguel County, the Sheridan Opera House, The Alibi, Wilkinson Library, KOTO, telluride.com, and more).

item.title: 📅 The Week Ahead — Oct 8–14
item.description: The biggest item this week is the San Miguel County Planning Commission's all-day meeting on October 8, which opens with a joint BOCC work session on an Affordable Housing Code Update — about as close to the root of this valley's housing crisis as any single agenda gets. SMART's board also meets virtually that same day to vote on amending the Gondola Project Development IGA for FY27 and to kick off budget talks over how to allocate $5.2 million a year in tax revenue. Elsewhere, a public hearing on special event liquor permits for the Telluride Horror Show lands October 14, and the Ballot Measure 5A Information Meeting on Monday is worth your time if you haven't sorted out where you stand on that one yet.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Planning Commission Meeting — 2026-10-08
item.description:
San Miguel County • 2026-10-08
The San Miguel County Planning Commission meets October 8 for a session that spans most of the day. The morning opens with a joint work session with the BOCC on an Affordable Housing Code Update — a signal that the county is still actively trying to write policy fast enough to keep pace with a housing situation that hasn't gotten easier. After lunch, the commission takes up a Land Use Code amendment covering Subdivisions and Condominium Plats, which would change the rules governing how land gets divided and how ownership gets structured across unincorporated county. Both items sit at the code-change tier — the kind of amendments that quietly shape what gets built, where, and for whom, long after the meeting is over.
⚡ Why it matters: Joint BOCC work session on Affordable Housing Code Update; public comment opportunity.

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] San Miguel Authority for Regional Transportation - Oct 08 2026 — 2026-10-08
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-10-08
SMART's board meets virtually October 8th with two consequential action items. Resolution 2026-22 would amend the Gondola Project Development IGA for FY27 — another formal step in the long-running effort to get the gondola funded and built. The board will also begin FY27 budget development discussions, which will shape how the authority spends the $5.2M/year in tax revenue voters approved under Measure 3A. A verbal gondola project update and the September operations report round out the substantive content. The meeting closes with an executive session covering two matters: personnel issues related to the Executive Director position, and legal counsel consultation on Masson vs. San Miguel County BOCC — a case worth watching for anyone tracking the gondola's legal and political landscape.
⚡ Why it matters: Vote on Gondola IGA amendment and FY27 budget direction for $5.2M in tax revenue.

item.title: [Thu, Oct 8] The Creative Exchange at Telluride Arts HQ
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Telluride Arts HQ, TELLURIDE The Creative Exchange is a brand-new monthly series by Telluride Arts designed for the artists and creatives who call Telluride home. It’s a space where emerging and established artists gather to share the knowledge, skills, and stories that fuel their work. Think of it as an open source model for creativity—where we learn from each other, swap ideas, and help strengthen one another’s practice. Each session is hosted by local artists and creative leaders who bring their own perspectives, techniques, and creative journeys into the room. Topics may span everything from the business of art and professional development, to creative process, storytelling, collaboration, and the philosophical underpinnings of making art. Whether you’re a full-time working artist, an educator, a student, a maker, or simply someone curious about creative expression, the Creative Exchange is open to you. …

item.title: [Fri, Oct 9] Cliff Allred featured at West End Stories & Poems at the Naturita Library Oct. 8th
item.description: 🎫 KOTO 📍 Naturita Community Library Leslie Ament of Naturita and Art Goodtimes of Wrights Mesa will be hosting Cliff Allred discussing all things paranormal Thursday, Oct. 8 th , at 6 pm MDT at the Naturita Community Library. “We will be talking about near death experiences, ghosts, unexplained encounters and other mysterious experiences,” said Allred, a Naturita resident and library employee. “Come share your stories with us.” Cliff was born in Craig, Colorado, and his parents moved to Naturita when he was in kindergarten. He went to college at Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University in Prescott, Arizona, in 2001, the same year he was diagnosed with cancer and underwent treatment. He graduated from college in 2006, moved to Phoenix, and worked there as a drafter for twelve years. In 2018 he moved back to Naturita and helped his parents build a house, then found a job at the library in 2020. …

item.title: ⚡ [Meeting] Special Liquor Licensing Authority - Oct 14 2026 — 2026-10-14
item.description:
Town of Telluride • 2026-10-14
One item of substance: a public hearing on three special event permits for Palm Arts Inc. to serve alcohol at the Palm Theatre (721 W. Colorado Ave.) during the Telluride Horror Show, October 16–18, 2026. Projected attendance runs 600 on Friday evening and 1,400 each on Saturday and Sunday. Staff recommends approval — the Marshal's Department has no concerns, and the applicant's paperwork checks out. The board will also approve minutes from the September 17 meeting.
⚡ Why it matters: Public hearing on Horror Show alcohol permits; 1,400-person weekend crowds at stake.
